# reac-repacer

reac-repacer is the de-jitter relay of FreeREAC: between a Wi-Fi link and the REAC stageboxes of a Roland mixer, it buffers the bursty stream of REAC audio frames and re-emits it at a steady cadence. The fuzz targets drive the code that reads bytes from the network and from its configuration. [FreeREAC/reac-repacer](https://github.com/FreeREAC/reac-repacer) · OSS-Fuzz: no project for reac-repacer

**Status: available.** Of reac-repacer's own fuzz targets, which OSS-Fuzz does not run, statements cover 4 of 4. 16 binaries, 4.9 MB. 28 statements: 20 proved, 0 known false, 0 suspected false, 0 blocked by the model, 8 open.

Built from reac-repacer 0.2.3 (commit `3ac1cf10`).

## At a glance
| harness | what it does | checks beyond "does not crash" | statements |
|---|---|---|---|
| [fuzz_wire](fuzz_wire/) | Takes one flag byte (the broadcast-only switch and a channel slot from -2 to 125) and then a frame, cut to the 1600 bytes of the daemon's receive buffer. It runs the frame through every reader the daemon applies to a frame from the wire: the forward classifier, the return relay, the downstream listener, the clock meter, the counter read, the channel-width rule, the tag-removing copy reader and the slot sample reader. It compares each answer with one the harness computes itself from the REAC frame layout. | 8 checks (reference-oracle; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 7 proved |
| [fuzz_egress](fuzz_egress/) | Takes a slot byte, a 32-bit output counter, twelve 32-bit samples and then a frame of at most 1600 bytes. It runs every write the daemon makes into a frame it emits: the counter restamp, the mute used during a rate change, the gate that decides whether a frame holds the injected slot, and the slot sample writer. It compares each resulting frame with one the harness builds itself from the REAC frame layout. | 4 checks (reference-oracle; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 3 proved |
| [fuzz_lock](fuzz_lock/) | Takes a rate selector byte, a name-length byte (its value modulo 16), an interface name of that many bytes (an empty name, or one holding a NUL, space, tab, CR or LF, is rejected), and then the text of a warm-start lock file. It asks the lock reader for the saved frame period of that interface at that rate, checks that the answer is the same when the byte after the text is "0" and when it is a space, and compares it with the period the harness finds itself by parsing the record grammar (port, period, rate label, within 5% of the standard period, last record wins, at most 65536 bytes). | 2 checks (invariant, reference-oracle; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 3 proved |
| [fuzz_uci](fuzz_uci/) | Takes a ring-size bit and then, for each of the five hot parameters, a running value and a configuration reply of up to 255 bytes. It reads each reply as an integer, checks that the value is the same when the byte after the reply is "0" and when it is a space, compares it with the value the harness parses itself, and then checks that holding the five values to their ranges gives the ranges the harness defines itself. | 3 checks (invariant, reference-oracle; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 7 proved |

## What the statements say, for reac-repacer
- **`<build>_halts`**: on every input on which the build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise: an input that needs more is not covered), and when the environment refuses nothing it is not forced to, every execution exits with status 0 or 2, without crashing, failing an assertion, hanging or tripping its sanitizer.
- **`<build>_agrees`**: on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding its budget (a premise), neither build reaches an error, and the two have the same set of observable behaviours: every sequence of writes and exit status one can show, the other can too. A sanitizer report aborts, so this rules out every error the sanitizer build's configuration detects. It does not rule out a run that never ends; only a halts statement does.

## Known issues
None known.

## Get and run the binaries
    ./oft fetch reac-repacer
    ./oft verify-sha reac-repacer

By hand: download `reac-repacer-bin.tar.zst` from release [v2026.11.1](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.11.1), unpack it into `projects/reac-repacer/bin/`, and check each file against its SHA-256 in the harness's `harness.yaml`. Each binary is run as `<file> <input-file>` under qemu-user 10; a testcase needs the six-byte header `00 00 00 00 00 00` in front ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)).

## How these binaries were built
- Library: [FreeREAC/reac-repacer](https://github.com/FreeREAC/reac-repacer) at `3ac1cf1017c847fe2272fce7f2f93306f8a23b42` (0.2.3), built with its own build scripts
- Harnesses: unmodified
- Everywhere: static riscv64 compiled for RV64G, musl, clang 20.1.8 with `-Os -g`, and a small driver that reads the input file ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)). The sanitizer flags and options are in [docs/building.md](../../docs/building.md). Each harness page lists what else its builds change, and which of its checks were confirmed in the binaries.
- Builder image: `ghcr.io/theorem-labs/oss-fuzz-theorems-toolchain@sha256:6a6b4816865c7ec61801ae0fcab6d9c81a599ffcb20616576a9c668abd8b0a7b`. The OSS Verify port `projects/reac-repacer` at `d897ff19667fd95fa86514cc2750b650b9845988` in `theorem-labs/oss-verify` built every binary of this project instead of a build recipe. Its archive [`reac-repacer-port.tar.zst`](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.11.1-src) holds the port's `tools/check`, which builds them again on this image with Docker: it fetches the project's source trees over the network, at the commits and SHA-256s the port pins, and does not read `reac-repacer-src.tar.zst` ([docs/reproducing.md](../../docs/reproducing.md)).

## Licence
reac-repacer is under `GPL-3.0-or-later`. Each binary is a combined work of reac-repacer, the harness, the C library, the compiler's runtime and every library it links; the SPDX expression of each is not recorded here yet. Corresponding source, in release [v2026.11.1-src](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.11.1-src): `reac-repacer-src.tar.zst`, the upstream source trees exactly as upstream publishes them; `reac-repacer-src.MANIFEST.tsv`, which says where the build lays each one down; and [`reac-repacer-port.tar.zst`](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.11.1-src), the port archive at `d897ff19667fd95fa86514cc2750b650b9845988` holding its `infra/`, `tools/` and `projects/reac-repacer/` files: the build scripts, and the source of the driver linked into these binaries. Its binaries are under a GPL-family licence, so their corresponding source also takes `toolchain-src.tar.zst`, the source of the toolchain they were built with, in release [sources-v1](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/sources-v1).
